spec: ProgressDesk MS3: durable progress. Named immutable checkpoints, a deterministic recovery packet, a split ladder that a too-large feature cannot escape, and a baseline that a completed phase replays into. The context a builder is handed is now feature-scoped, so each feature names the approved specification excerpts it needs.

acceptanceConditions: a checkpoint manifest names the project, the journal sequence it was derived from, the definition references in force, the accepted artifact manifest, the tool, skill and domain version references in force, the task and milestone state and the pending actions
a checkpoint is immutable, a second checkpoint with the same name is refused, and a milestone boundary creates one

the recovery packet names the current task, the accepted baseline, surviving candidate artifacts, completed actions, unresolved effects, failed checks, remaining work and the allowance, and carries no role transcript
the same checkpoint and project produce the same recovery packet
a feature that does not deliver is split, and split again, until it is delivered or unsplittable
a completed phase replays into a deterministic baseline of measured usage, with unmeasured values left unknown
the context a builder receives names the approved specification excerpts the feature asked for, and the milestone gate still judges the whole accepted contract

features.title: Named immutable checkpoints
features.outcome: ProgressDesk can create and list named immutable checkpoints, on command and at a milestone boundary. Each manifest records the project, the journal sequence it was derived from, the definition references in force, the accepted artifact manifest, the tool, skill and domain version references in force, the task and milestone state, and the pending actions.
features.scope: A new module src/progressdesk/checkpoints.py and the route table in src/progressdesk/runtime.py. Reuse the existing event log and artifact store; do not create a second store and do not change the event vocabulary.
interfaces: route verb 'checkpoint.create' with params project_id, name -> manifest with keys checkpointId, projectId, name, journalSequence, definitionRefs, acceptedArtifactManifestRef, toolSkillDomainVersionRefs, taskAndMilestoneStateRef, pendingActionRefs, createdAt
a milestone boundary creates a checkpoint of that milestone
acceptance: a created checkpoint manifest contains every named field
its journalSequence is the sequence of the last event read when it was created
creating a checkpoint with a name that already exists is refused and records nothing
checkpoint.list returns the checkpoints of that project only, oldest first
a milestone boundary creates a checkpoint without a separate command

features.title: The deterministic recovery packet
features.outcome: A fresh worker can continue recorded work from a recovery packet that names the current task, the accepted baseline, surviving candidate artifacts, completed actions, unresolved effects, failed checks, remaining work and the remaining allowance. It is assembled deterministically, without a model, and it carries no private model reasoning and no role transcript.
features.scope: A new module src/progressdesk/recovery.py and the route table in src/progressdesk/runtime.py. Read the event log and the artifact store only.
interfaces: route verb 'recovery.packet' with params project_id and optional checkpoint_id -> packet with keys projectId, checkpointId, currentTask, acceptedBaseline, survivingCandidateArtifacts, completedActions, unresolvedEffects, failedChecks, remainingWork, allowance
acceptance: the packet names the current task and the remaining allowance
the packet lists the accepted artifact references and the surviving candidate artifacts
no role transcript appears in the packet
the same checkpoint and project produce the same packet
building the packet records no model or tool execution

features.title: A feature that does not deliver is split, and split again
features.outcome: A feature that does not deliver is split into two ordinary features, and a half that still does not deliver is split again, until the work is delivered or the feature is unsplittable. The cause of the non-delivery is the splitter's evidence, not a reason to stop the ladder.
features.scope: Only src/progressdesk/loop.py. The split itself already exists in src/progressdesk/jack.py and src/progressdesk/feature_list.py; this is the entry that routes a non-delivery into it.
interfaces: a round that ends without a delivery enters the split path
a capacity refusal is not a work outcome and pauses instead of splitting
acceptance: a round that was cut off short is split rather than abandoned
an applied split leaves two ordinary features in the plan
a capacity refusal does not split the feature
the split context carries the feature's own contract and the milestone's obligations

features.title: A completed phase replays into a deterministic baseline
features.outcome: A completed phase replays into a baseline: the recorded usage of every actual execution, with only measured values and unknown ones left unknown. Replaying the same phase twice gives the same baseline, and the baseline names no score, no ranking and no goal - a target is the owner's to set, and only after a baseline exists.
features.scope: A new read-only module src/progressdesk/baseline.py and the route table in src/progressdesk/runtime.py.
interfaces: route verb 'baseline.replay' with params project_id -> {'phase': str, 'rows': [...], 'totals': {...}}
one row per recorded execution of the phase
acceptance: the baseline holds one row per recorded usage event of the phase
an unmeasured value stays null and is never a zero
replaying the same phase twice gives the same baseline
the baseline contains no score, ranking or goal value
